 Order

This petition, under Article 227 of the Constitution of India, has been filed against the order dated 16.01.2018 passed by Second Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Damoh in MACC No.38/2015, by which the application filed by the petitioner under Order 1 Rule 10(2) of CPC has been rejected.

entities.text: Second Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Damoh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The facts necessary for disposal of the present petition in short, are that one Madan alias Kariya died in a vehicular accident, which took place on 08.09.2015 on account of head-on collision between two motorcycles.
It was the case of the claimants that the Driver of the motorcycle bearing registration no.MP20 P 0160 has caused the accident by driving the same in a rash and negligent manner.
Undisputedly, the motorcycle bearing registration no.MP20 P 0160 was registered in the name of the petitioner.
Accordingly, the claim petition was filed against the driver of the motorcycle namely Mukesh Dubey as well as the petitioner.

The petitioner filed an application under Order 1 Rule 10(2) of CPC on the ground that he had already sold the offending motorcycle to Jabalpur Auto Deal owned by one Mohd.Shaban on consideration of Rs.11,500/-.

It appears that the aforesaid Auto Deal has sold the vehicle to Shri Amit Dubey for a sale consideration of Rs.16,551/- and, therefore, it was pleaded that Mohd.Shaban and Amit Dubey may also be impleaded as defendants.
3. By the impugned order, the said application has been rejected.
4. Challenging the order passed by the Claims Tribunal, it is submitted by the counsel for the petitioner that it is true that the petitioner was a registered owner but once he had already alienated the motorcycle, then he is not responsible to pay compensation to the claimants and, therefore, the actual owner was a necessary party and the Claims Tribunal should have allowed the application.
5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner.
6. Undisputedly, the petitioner was the registered owner of the offending motorcycle on the date of the incident.
7.
The submission made by the counsel for the petitioner is no more res integra.

8. The Supreme Court in the case of Surendra Kumar Bhilawe Vs. New India Assurance Co.Ltd.,
reported in 2020 (18) SCC 224 has held as under :-

entities.text:
Surendra Kumar Bhilawe Vs. New India Assurance Co.Ltd.,
reported in 2020 (18) SCC 224
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It would also be pertinent to note the difference between the definition of "owner" in Section 2(30) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the definition of "owner" in Section 2(19) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1939 which has been repealed and replaced by the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Under the old Act "owner" meant the person in possession of a motor vehicle.
The definition has undergone a change.
The legislature has consciously changed the definition of "owner" to mean the person in whose name the motor vehicle stands.
39. The finding of the National Commission that the fact of registration of the said truck in the name of the appellant was inconsequential is also not sustainable in law.
Section 2(30) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 defines "owner" to mean the person in whose name the motor vehicle stands registered.
The definition of "owner" has been overlooked and ignored by the National Commission.

Had ownership of the said truck intended to be transferred forthwith, the registration would have been transferred in the name of the transferee, as also the permit to operate the said truck for carriage of goods."
9.
Thus, the owner of the vehicle means the person in whose name the motor vehicle was registered.
Since the petitioner is the registered owner of the offending motorcycle, therefore, he cannot say that the person to whom he had sold the vehicle, is also a necessary party.
10. Furthermore, the claimants are the dominus litis.
A defendant cannot move an application for impleading others as co-defendants.
If the defendant successfully establishes that the necessary party was not impleaded, then it is for the claimant to face the consequences.
But the case cannot be conducted as per the wishes of the defendant.
11. As no jurisdictional error was committed by the Claims Tribunal, accordingly, the petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
12. This Court by order dated 07.02.2018 had stayed the further proceedings.
Unfortunately, this petition has remained pending for more than 5 long years specifically when the claimants had lost their bread earner.
13. Accordingly, the Claims Tribunal is directed to decide the claim petition positively within a period of 6 months from today.
If necessary, the Claims Tribunal shall proceed on day-to-day basis and shall not grant any adjournment to either of the parties without any reason.
Furthermore, no adjournment beyond the period of 7 days shall be granted.

(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE TG /-
